root_cause.text: In F2FS atomic fsync, f2fs_fsync_node_pages() computed and set the inode folio’s dentry mark before __write_node_folio() acquired sbi->node_write, allowing a concurrent checkpoint to update nat_entry->IS_CHECKPOINTED after the check and making the folio state inconsistent with checkpoint completion.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly describes Thread A calling f2fs_need_dentry_mark() before __write_node_folio() blocks on f2fs_down_read(&sbi->node_write), while Thread B concurrently runs f2fs_write_checkpoint() and sets {struct nat_entry}->flag |= BIT(IS_CHECKPOINTED); the fix moves set_dentry_mark() for atomic writes out of f2fs_fsync_node_pages() and into __write_node_folio() under the node_write synchronization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update atomic node folio writes to preserve barrier behavior and also set dentry marks for inode folios when needed.
intent_record.what: The single-line conditional that only added REQ_PREFLUSH | REQ_FUA when atomic and NOBARRIER was not set was expanded into an atomic-only block that still conditionally sets those write flags and additionally, for inode folios, calls set_dentry_mark(folio, f2fs_need_dentry_mark(sbi, ino_of_node(folio))).
intent_record.how: At runtime, atomic node folio writes continue to use flush/FUA barriers when enabled, and now inode folios written in the atomic path also have their dentry mark updated based on f2fs_need_dentry_mark(). This ensures extra metadata state is recorded during atomic writes rather than being skipped for inode node folios.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip dentry marking during atomic fsync in f2fs_fsync_node_pages to avoid incorrect metadata updates in atomic mode.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to set_dentry_mark(folio, f2fs_need_dentry_mark(sbi, ino)) inside f2fs_fsync_node_pages() was changed to execute only when the atomic condition is false by wrapping it in an if (!atomic) block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, dentry marking is now skipped during atomic fsync paths, while preserved for non-atomic cases. This prevents the function from updating dentry mark state when operating in atomic mode, avoiding behavior that was previously applied in all cases.

grouping_result.intent: Update atomic node folio writes to preserve barrier behavior and also set dentry marks for inode folios when needed.
Skip dentry marking during atomic fsync in f2fs_fsync_node_pages to avoid incorrect metadata updates in atomic mode.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly modifies atomic node folio writes and adds setting dentry marks for inode folios during that path, which matches the vulnerable area where dentry marking for inode folios in atomic fsync/write sequencing was done at the wrong time relative to node_write/checkpointing.

The change directly alters dentry marking behavior in f2fs_fsync_node_pages during atomic fsync, which is the exact area implicated by the root cause: incorrect/inconsistent dentry mark setting in atomic fsync relative to checkpoint state updates.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct state mutation identified in the root cause: during atomic fsync, the inode folio's dentry mark was set before __write_node_folio() took sbi->node_write, so a concurrent checkpoint could change checkpointed state after this mark decision and leave the folio inconsistent.

This computes the dentry-mark decision outside the protected write path. Because the checkpoint state could change concurrently before node_write locking, this check could become stale and cause the incorrect mark to be applied.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the inode folio dentry-mark state mutation before __write_node_folio() acquires sbi->node_write. That ordering creates the race described in the root cause, where a concurrent checkpoint can change checkpointed state after the mark decision, leaving folio state inconsistent with checkpoint completion.

This statement computes the dentry-mark decision outside the protected node write path. Because checkpoint state may change concurrently before sbi->node_write is taken, this result can become stale and directly contributes to the incorrect folio marking in atomic fsync.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function body is shown: `int f2fs_fsync_node_pages(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi, struct inode *inode, struct writeback_control *wbc, bool atomic)`. Inside it, for inode pages, the code does `set_dentry_mark(page, f2fs_need_dentry_mark(sbi, ino));` before the page write path is invoked. Later the page is written through `f2fs_wait_on_page_writeback(page, NODE, true);` and then `err = __write_node_page(page, atomic, &submitted, wbc, true, FS_NODE_IO);`. In `__write_node_page`, the lock acquisition happens only later: `if (atomic && !test_opt(sbi, NOBARRIER)) { ... down_read(&sbi->node_write); }` and only after that `f2fs_get_node_info(sbi, nid, &ni);` and the write proceed. This matches the root cause: dentry mark is computed/set in fsync before `__write_node_page()` acquires `sbi->node_write`, so a concurrent checkpoint can change checkpointed NAT state between `f2fs_need_dentry_mark()` and the actual protected write. There is no added synchronization around `f2fs_need_dentry_mark()` in `f2fs_fsync_node_pages`, and no movement of the dentry-mark logic under `sbi->node_write` in this snippet. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present.
